videos.script: Lesson eleven wrote a small vector store by hand, to see what one has to do. This lesson meets three real ones: Chroma, Pinecone and Weaviate. {{three}} Chroma runs here, inside a Python program, and keeps everything in one directory. {{chroma}} You will load the forty help-centre articles into it without computing a single vector. Chroma runs the same small model you have used since lesson one. {{load}} Then you will ask it the customer's question and read what comes back. Not scores. Distances. {{distances}} The same three articles get three sets of numbers in three spaces. A cut-off written for one of them is wrong for the others. {{spaces}} You will open the directory and find a SQLite file with a log of every write, and an index beside it. Then you will serve the same directory over HTTP. {{disk}} Pinecone and Weaviate do not run on this machine. Pinecone is only a hosted service. Weaviate's embedded mode downloads a program this lab cannot reach. {{hosted}} So their code is shown as written for their clients, and never run. The ideas carry over: a dimension and a metric fixed at the start, records with metadata, a query with a filter. {{code}} The lesson ends on the question that outlasts any one product. Who runs it, and who pays for what. {{compare}}
